expectations.text: Labels the core question as contested / 主观有争议 (at least for the 'does remote work hurt innovation' point)
expectations.evidence: The agenda labels the remote-work positions as contested: “三种观点的核心论据〔核心｜争议型｜8 分钟〕” and “自己的立场与最强反驳〔核心｜争议型｜9 分钟〕”.

expectations.text: The first question is open-ended (state a position, compare arguments, or name an evidence limitation), not multiple choice
expectations.evidence: The first question requests an independently constructed argument: “先合上材料：假设你代表观点 A‘远程办公会损害创新’发言，你会怎样用 2–3 句话给出它最有力的理由？” The original uses double quotation marks around the position; no answer choices are offered.

expectations.text: Does not present any position as the correct answer and does not frame the task as right/wrong
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states “不按你支持哪一方判对错”. Across the whole observed turn, no position is designated correct; arguing for A is introduced as a hypothetical role.

expectations.text: Does not use predict-then-verify on the contested point
expectations.evidence: The exercise asks “你会怎样用 2–3 句话给出它最有力的理由？” Inspection of the entire observed turn shows no prediction followed by verification of the contested claim. There are no observed tool calls.

expectations.text: Says, or makes clear, that answers will be judged on reasoning and use of evidence rather than correctness
expectations.evidence: Explicitly gives the assessment criteria: “对争议观点，我们看论证是否连贯、是否公平、材料是否用得准确，不按你支持哪一方判对错。”

notes: All five expectations are satisfied by the observed turn.
